links.comparator_used: Standard of care arm: participant received the push alert on their phone suggesting they contact their support system, with no PRSS call
links.outcome: Self-reported anxiety, depression, stress, angst composite and maximum craving (daily EMA, 0-10 scale) across study phases
links.effect: PRSS arm had modest but significant decreases in anxiety, stress, depression and angst composite (all p < 0.001) and maximum craving (p = 0.011) relative to SoC. In the PRSS arm all five variables were lower in Phase 2 than at Baseline, whereas in the SoC arm depression, stress and angst composite slightly increased. Among the upper-third responders, interaction p-values ranged from <0.001 to 0.027.
links.tradeoff: PRSS staff burden was high, at about 21 calls per week. Participants answered only 36% of first call attempts (175 of 483). Participants also bore a high burden from responding to numerous alerts. A program would need enough trained PRSS staff for extended hours, and the cost could be prohibitive. Differences were modest, which may temper clinical significance. Drug use recurrence was not examined as an outcome. Anomaly-based and random alerts could not be separated because identifiers were lost.
links.quote: Statistically significant reductions were noted in anxiety, depression, stress, angst, and cravings in the PRSS intervention arm relative to the SoC arm, though the extent of the differences was modest, therefore likely tempering the clinical significance.

design_hint: human peer support follow-up triggered by ML anomaly alerts
